title: Email, identidad y aprobación humana
review_contracts: PYARCANA — MODO REVISOR ESCÉPTICO Y ANTI-COMPLACENCIA
Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

prior_audit.method: Direct fetch of audit/lessons-only/sections/S22.json returned 404 before creation.

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only prior concepts adjudicated USABLE count as learned.
learner_entry_state.critical_dependency_warning: S21 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED. Its reconciled package, artifact hashes, pending_review manifest, PDF accessibility and cross-artifact parity cannot be inherited as trustworthy.
usable: human approval should remain separate from automated generation
semantic headings and non-color redundancy as accessibility principles
not_creditable: S21 manifest is persisted and derived from actual artifacts
S21 pending_review state is bound to exact files
S21 monetary values have preserved the S02 Decimal boundary

roadmap_expectation.T1: Mensaje: MIME, encoding, HTML/text y attachments; templates y sanitización
roadmap_expectation.T2: Proveedor: OAuth/service account y scopes; drafts, expiración y adaptadores
roadmap_expectation.T3: Destinatario: resolución y verificación; listas, CC/BCC, privacidad y mínima divulgación
roadmap_expectation.T4: Workflow: approval queue y state machine; idempotencia, audit log y reintento sin duplicar
roadmap_expectation.gate: crea borradores en sandbox o .eml; ningún correo real se envía automáticamente y todo destinatario requiere confirmación

live_site.evidence: Public page exposes Section 22 'Email y aprobación' with the canonical draft-only tagline. Hydrated theory body is not present in the text surface, so render-only defects remain unresolved.

checks: sanitize_html with allowed_hosts={'corp.pe'} still permits https://sub.example.pe/r because .example.pe is hardcoded
sanitize_html blocks a documented relative route such as /review/r1
OrderedDict dedupe keeps first position but replaces the first recipient record/role with the last duplicate
approval state machine allows actor='analyst' to submit and then approve the same draft
recipient regex accepts whitespace and newline-containing local parts
idempotency key is unchanged when subject/attachments change unless body_ver is manually changed

external_research.finding: gmail.compose manages drafts and sends emails; draft-only must therefore be enforced by application policy.
Apps should request only the smallest scopes needed and handle granted scopes explicitly.
Bcc hides Bcc addresses from other recipients; To/Cc remain destination headers and Bcc handling is implementation-dependent.
.test, .example, .invalid and reserved example.com/net/org are special-use; example.pe is not reserved.
Email messages should be treated as structured MIME trees; high-level EmailMessage APIs can inspect multipart structure semantically.

findings.title: UNTRUSTED_S21_PACKAGE_ASSUMED_RECONCILED
findings.evidence: S22 repeatedly says the S21 report package is already reconciled and uses its run data as input.
findings.impact: S21 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED; its parity/provenance/pending_review evidence is not creditable. S22 can therefore package or route an unverified report.

findings.title: ROUTABLE_EXAMPLE_PE_USED_AS_LAB_EMAIL_DOMAIN
findings.evidence: The lab allowlists and addresses use @example.pe and explicitly say it is not an impossible-to-route domain.
findings.impact: RFC/IANA reserve .test/.example/.invalid and example.com/net/org, not example.pe. A future provider adapter could accidentally address a real domain, contradicting the no-real-email gate.

findings.title: EMAIL_IRREVERSIBILITY_OVERCLAIM
findings.evidence: Opening says an email 'no se puede deshacer'.
findings.impact: Recall/retraction mechanisms exist in limited systems; the transferable rule is that delivery cannot be reliably revoked once a recipient/provider has received the message.

findings.title: BCC_PRIVACY_MODEL_INCOMPLETE_FOR_EXTERNAL_RECIPIENTS
findings.evidence: The section treats moving externals to BCC as a privacy protection for the recipient list.
findings.impact: BCC hides BCC addresses from other recipients, but BCC recipients normally still receive visible To/Cc headers. Individual sends are required when an external must not learn internal recipient addresses.

findings.title: ATTACHMENT_DESCRIBED_AS_CONTROLLED_DISCLOSURE_SURFACE
findings.evidence: T3-B suggests sensitive detail can live in a 'controlled attachment' instead of the body.
findings.impact: An email attachment is copied to the recipient and can be forwarded; it is not equivalent to an access-controlled portal. Disclosure minimization must cover attachments too.

findings.title: MIME_HEADER_COUNT_FALSE_GREEN
findings.evidence: T1-A says counting Content-Type headers validates that the multipart tree is correctly nested.
findings.impact: The number of Content-Type headers does not prove multipart/alternative placement, attachment disposition, or part semantics; different trees can have the same count.

findings.title: PLAIN_TEXT_PRESENTED_AS_PROTOCOL_MANDATORY
findings.evidence: Figure/callout say the plain-text part is 'not optional' and many clients/filters require it.
findings.impact: multipart/alternative text+HTML is strong compatibility practice, but an HTML-only MIME message is not categorically invalid. Teach it as a robustness/accessibility requirement of the course, not a universal protocol law.

findings.title: SANITIZER_ALLOWED_HOSTS_PARAMETER_BYPASSED_BY_HARDCODED_SUFFIX
findings.evidence: sanitize_html accepts allowed_hosts but also always permits host.endswith('.example.pe').
findings.impact: Passing allowed_hosts={'corp.pe'} still permits sub.example.pe. The security parameter does not actually define the policy.

findings.title: RELATIVE_LINK_POLICY_CONTRADICTS_IMPLEMENTATION
findings.evidence: T1-B says relative routes are allowed, but sanitize_html only permits URLs matching ^https?://.
findings.impact: A documented allowed class is always blocked, making the contract and code disagree.

findings.title: DRAFT_ONLY_LEAST_PRIVILEGE_CHECK_ACCEPTS_SEND
findings.evidence: least_privilege_ok treats mail.send as part of the allowed capability set and only excludes mail.full.
findings.impact: A granted ['mail.draft','mail.send'] evaluates True even though the callout says deny mail.send for a draft-only lab.

findings.title: SCOPE_POLICY_IS_HARDCODED_NOT_OBSERVED
findings.evidence: Prose says requested∩allowed and granted scopes are audited, but the example hardcodes requested_scopes/granted_scopes and never validates a provider response or fail-closes on missing/unexpected grants.
findings.impact: Learners can print least_privilege_ok without demonstrating that authorization actually matches policy.

findings.title: DRAFT_EXPIRY_NOT_INTEGRATED_WITH_APPROVAL_STATE
findings.evidence: T2-B says expired drafts cannot be promoted without regeneration/reapproval; T4 approval state machine never checks draft expiry or draft usability.
findings.impact: An approval can remain 'approved' after the underlying draft expires or changes.

findings.title: FILE_DRAFT_ADAPTER_IS_MEMORY_ONLY_AND_MISSING_IDS_CRASH
findings.evidence: FileDraftAdapter stores drafts only in a dict and is_usable directly indexes self.store[draft_id].
findings.impact: The name suggests file persistence that does not exist, and an unknown ID raises KeyError instead of an explicit not-found/unusable result.

findings.title: RECIPIENT_FORMAT_CHECK_ACCEPTS_WHITESPACE_AND_CONTROL_SHAPES
findings.evidence: verify uses ^[^@]+@[^@]+\.[^@]+$ as a 'bad_format' gate.
findings.impact: It accepts strings such as 'a b@example.pe' and even newline-containing local parts. A basic gate should at least reject whitespace/control characters or use a standard parser.

findings.title: DECLARED_CANDIDATE_RECIPIENT_STATE_NEVER_EXISTS
findings.evidence: Prose defines unresolved → candidate → verified|rejected.
findings.impact: The implementation jumps directly from directory lookup to verified/rejected; candidate is not represented or audited.

findings.title: DEDUPE_OVERWRITES_FIRST_RECIPIENT_ROLE
findings.evidence: T3-B promises dedupe preserving first appearance, but OrderedDict assignment replaces the value for a duplicate email.
findings.impact: A later duplicate can change a first BCC entry into To/CC and increase disclosure while preserving the original position.

findings.title: EXTERNAL_RECIPIENT_POLICY_HARDCODED_TO_OTHER_TEST
findings.evidence: T3-B says every external domain is forced to BCC, but code only checks email.endswith('@other.test').
findings.impact: Any other external domain remains visible, so the policy does not generalize beyond the fixture.

findings.title: LIST_SIZE_AND_OPTOUT_CONTRACT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
findings.evidence: T3-B says the lab models a list-size cap and synthetic opt-out flag.
findings.impact: Neither appears in the canonical theory code, so two announced privacy controls are prose-only.

findings.title: APPROVER_ROLE_NOT_AUTHORIZED
findings.evidence: approval_sm.py accepts any actor string for approve.
findings.impact: The same analyst who submitted can call approve and reach approved. 'Human approval' is not equivalent to an authorized independent reviewer.

findings.title: APPROVAL_AUDIT_MISSING_TIMESTAMP_AND_COMMENTS
findings.evidence: The transition log stores from/to/action/actor only.
findings.impact: S21 carry-forward and S22 prose require actor, timestamp and review comments/notes; these are necessary to reconstruct who approved what and when.

findings.title: APPROVAL_NOT_BOUND_TO_EXACT_DRAFT_CONTENT
findings.evidence: Approval transitions contain no draft_id, message hash, recipient set, subject, attachment hashes or body version.
findings.impact: A message can be edited after approval without invalidating the approval record. Human review must bind to the exact bytes/payload reviewed.

findings.title: EVERY_RECIPIENT_CONFIRMATION_GATE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
findings.evidence: Tagline says every recipient requires confirmation, but the state machine approves one draft state with no per-recipient confirmation evidence.
findings.impact: A multi-recipient draft can be approved without showing that each To/Cc/Bcc address was reviewed.

findings.title: IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OMITS_MESSAGE_PAYLOAD_FIELDS
findings.evidence: Key is sha256(run_id|to|body_ver)[:16].
findings.impact: Subject, body content hash, Cc/Bcc, attachments, sender and recipient-set version are absent; changed content can reuse an old draft if body_ver is not manually bumped.

findings.title: TRUNCATED_NONATOMIC_KEY_CANNOT_GUARANTEE_IDEMPOTENCY
findings.evidence: Outcome says 'Garantizar idempotencia' using sha256[:16] and a normal dict check-then-insert.
findings.impact: Sixteen hex characters are a 64-bit prefix and there is no collision check or atomic uniqueness. Concurrent workers can also race through the membership check.

findings.title: IDEMPOTENCY_AUDIT_LOG_LACKS_ACTOR_TIMESTAMP_AND_STATE
findings.evidence: T4-B says audit log records create/submit/approve/retry_hit with actor and timestamps in production; example only logs create/retry_hit with key/draft_id.
findings.impact: The final idempotency example does not satisfy its own audit-log outcome or connect to the approval log.

findings.title: NO_INTEGRATED_PERSISTED_DRAFT_APPROVAL_WORKFLOW
findings.evidence: Theory examples separately demonstrate MIME, sanitizer, scopes, draft store, recipients, list hygiene, approval and key.
findings.impact: No executable flow consumes a validated S21 manifest, creates a persisted .eml/sandbox draft, binds verified recipients, submits it, records approval, checks expiry/idempotency and persists one audit trail. The section gate is therefore not demonstrated end-to-end.

findings.title: SPANGLISH_AND_WIDOW_TERM_DENSITY
findings.evidence: Learner-facing prose rapidly stacks draft, sandbox, fail-closed, scope, key, store, workflow, allowlist, BCC, HITL and audit log.
findings.impact: Several are glossed, but density remains high for ZERO_TECH and Spanish-first guidance can be more consistent.

findings.title: GENERIC_LINK_TEXT_WEAKENS_EMAIL_ACCESSIBILITY
findings.evidence: Sanitizer emits enlace for every permitted review URL.
findings.impact: Generic repeated link text gives little destination/purpose context to screen-reader and skim users; the reviewed action should have meaningful link text such as 'Revisar borrador del run …'.

rejected_false_positives: Gmail gmail.compose was claimed to allow send as well as drafts. REJECTED as a finding: current Google scope documentation confirms this.
Using email.mime classes is automatically obsolete/invalid. REJECTED: the compatibility API remains supported; the issue is weak validation, not mere API age.
BCC provides no privacy benefit. REJECTED: RFC 5322 explicitly defines Bcc to hide Bcc addresses; the defect is treating it as sufficient to hide visible To/Cc from an external Bcc recipient.
Any similarity score in recipient resolution is unethical. REJECTED: S22 explicitly says matching is not fraud/identity proof and limits it to delivery review.
S22 secretly sends real email. REJECTED: no canonical theory path invokes SMTP/send; the risk is the use of a non-reserved domain if a future provider adapter is attached.
Service-account domain-wide delegation is inherently wrong. REJECTED: it is a valid Workspace pattern; the concern is least privilege and explicit impersonation.
priority_order: P1 safety gate: F02, F10-F12, F19-F26
HTML/MIME and address validation: F06-F09, F14
Upstream integrity: F01 and exact S21 manifest validation

USABLE: gmail.compose can send, so draft-only requires app policy
draft expiration as a freshness concept
invalid state transitions should fail closed
MISCONCEPTION_RISK: example.pe is a safe non-routable lab domain
BCC hides visible To/Cc from external Bcc recipients
dedupe preserves the first recipient policy
human actor string proves authorized approval
approval remains valid if draft changes/expires
